candidates.name: @a2ui/react (Google, A2UI v0.9+)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Production-grade A2UI React renderer that UAR can vendor and extend with the UAR-validated catalog (§10).

evidence.claim: v0.9 (April 2026) shipped an official React renderer wrapping @a2ui/web_core/MessageProcessor
v0.9.1 is current production; v1.0-rc was last updated June 8, 2026

risks: v1.0-rc is still iterating; vendor @a2ui/web_core (the framework-agnostic processor) instead of @a2ui/react to insulate from renderer breaks
UAR's approved catalog (9 components) is more restrictive than Google's; mapping work is required
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt and vendor @a2ui/web_core; build a UAR-owned React renderer on top, cross-test against @a2ui/react as reference impl.

candidates.name: LangChain Streaming Cookbook pattern
candidates.fit_for_gap: SDK design pattern: v2 typed StreamPart, framework SDKs for React/Angular/Svelte/Vue, examples for messages/values/custom modes.

evidence.claim: Runnable streaming examples across LangGraph, LangChain, React, Angular, Svelte, Vue; custom:a2ui channel pattern

risks: Pattern only; UAR must implement, not adopt
candidates.decision_rationale: The bar UAR's SDKs must clear; informs §2's per-language SDK design.

candidates.name: eventsource-client (TypeScript SSE)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Battle-tested SSE client for the TypeScript SDK's streaming chat / runs / events surfaces.

evidence.claim: Microsoft's @microsoft/fetch-event-source is the de-facto SSE client for browser-based TypeScript SDKs

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt for TS SDK SSE; pair with zod for typed event parsing.

candidates.name: sse-stream (Rust SSE client)
candidates.fit_for_gap: SSE streaming for the Rust SDK's chat / runs / events surfaces.

evidence.claim: reqwest-eventsource is the de-facto Rust SSE client built on reqwest

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; pair with typed deserialization via serde + thiserror for typed event variants.

candidates.name: zod (TypeScript runtime validation + types)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Typed error model + request/response validation for the TypeScript SDK.

evidence.claim: Zod 3.x is the dominant TS validation library; pairs with TS discriminated unions for error types

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt for TS SDK type system; codegen from UAR's JSON Schema via quicktype (§10).

candidates.name: pydantic (Python data validation + types)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Python SDK type system, structured output model class, settings management.

evidence.claim: Pydantic v2 is the dominant Python data validation library; required dependency of the LangChain Python SDK

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt for Python SDK; pairs with httpx for async HTTP.

candidates.name: miette (Rust typed-error pretty-printing)
candidates.fit_for_gap: SDK-side pretty-printing of the UarError chain (§5) for the Rust SDK.

evidence.claim: Miette is the 2026 standard for typed Rust error display; integrates with thiserror via Source

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt as the Rust SDK's error-display layer; central UarError implements Diagnostic.

candidates.name: figment (Rust layered config)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Layered configuration (env + file + CLI + defaults) with hot-reload support.

evidence.claim: Figment powers Rocket's config; battle-tested; supports hot-reload via Figment::merge

risks: Alternative to config crate; team is more familiar with config (the official intermodal crate)
candidates.decision_rationale: Alternative to config; config wins on name recognition but figment has nicer hot-reload story. Final pick: config + manual watch.

candidates.name: config (Rust config + ConfigLayer derive)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Standard Rust config crate; ConfigLayer derive reduces boilerplate; pairs with serde for typed config.

evidence.claim: config-rs is the de-facto Rust config crate; ConfigLayer derive (0.14+) reduces boilerplate

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; replace hand-written #[arg(env=...)] structs in src/config.rs.

candidates.name: secrecy (typed secret wrapper)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Wrap UAR_SECURITY__JWT_SECRET and provider API keys in Secret<String> to prevent accidental log/display.

evidence.claim: secrecy is the standard typed-secret crate; zero-cost, prevents accidental Debug/Display leakage

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt for every secret-typed field in config.

candidates.name: schemars (JSON Schema generation)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Generate JSON Schema from Rust types; produces the canonical config schema that the SDKs (§2) consume.

evidence.claim: schemars 0.8+ generates JSON Schema from serde types; used by apistos, aide, utoipa

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; one source of truth for the canonical config schema.

candidates.name: notify (file watching for hot-reload)
candidates.fit_for_gap: File watcher for config.yaml hot-reload.

evidence.claim: notify is the standard Rust file-watching crate; cross-platform; used by cargo

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; pair with arc-swap for lock-free hot-reload swap.

candidates.name: arc-swap (lock-free hot-reload)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Atomic swap of Arc'd config snapshots; readers never block writers.

evidence.claim: arc-swap is the standard lock-free Arc swap; readers never block

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; pair with notify for hot-reload.

candidates.name: vaultrs (Vault API client)
candidates.fit_for_gap: HashiCorp Vault client; allows UAR_SECURITY__JWT_SECRET and provider keys to live in Vault with a feature flag.

evidence.claim: vaultrs is the only mature Rust Vault client; supports KV v1/v2, transit, auth

risks: Adds a network dependency; only active with --features vault
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt behind a feature flag; documents the threat model in docs/configuration.md.

candidates.name: ragas (RAG evaluation framework)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Standard RAG evaluation: faithfulness, answer_relevancy, context_precision, context_recall (4 dimensions).

evidence.claim: RAGAS 0.x is the dominant open-source RAG evaluation framework; LLM-as-judge with frozen prompts
RAGAS, TruLens, and DeepEval are the three most widely adopted open-source RAG evaluation frameworks

risks: LLM-as-judge noise — must freeze prompt + model + version
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt as primary eval framework; pair with DeepEval as second opinion.

candidates.name: deepeval (RAG evaluation second opinion)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Second-opinion RAG evaluation; contextual relevancy, contextual precision/recall, answer relevancy, faithfulness.

evidence.claim: DeepEval provides 5+ RAG metrics covering retriever and generator independently

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt as second opinion; cross-validates RAGAS scores in CI.

candidates.name: trulens-eval (RAG Triad evaluation)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Alternative eval framework; RAG Triad (context relevance, groundedness, answer relevance).

evidence.claim: TruLens pioneered the RAG Triad; instrumentation-based with OpenTelemetry tracing

candidates.decision_rationale: Reference only; RAGAS + DeepEval cover the need.

candidates.name: beir (retrieval benchmark)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Standardized retrieval evaluation; BEIR scifact/nfcorpus/fiqa for public benchmark numbers.

evidence.claim: BEIR is the standard retrieval benchmark; 18+ datasets; used by every major RAG framework

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt for public benchmark numbers in docs/rag-benchmark/.

candidates.name: fastembed-rs (already adopted) + 4 more embedding backends
candidates.fit_for_gap: Currently single Tier-1 embedding (FastEmbed); add candle-embeddings, OpenAI, Voyage, Cohere.

evidence.claim: fastembed-rs is the de-facto Rust local-embedding crate; ONNX-backed

risks: Hosted backends (OpenAI/Voyage/Cohere) need API keys and rate-limit handling
candidates.decision_rationale: Keep fastembed-rs; add 4 more backends; document each in product-support-matrix.json.

candidates.name: thiserror 2.0 (already adopted, extend)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Library-side typed error enums; one UarError per module, #[non_exhaustive], #[source] chains.

evidence.claim: thiserror 2.0 is the standard for library error types; #[non_exhaustive] + #[source] + #[from] is the canonical pattern

candidates.decision_rationale: Keep; convert public-API anyhow!() to thiserror; add the central UarError.

candidates.name: anyhow 1.0 (already adopted, restrict)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Application-side error context; restrict to main / CLI code; remove from public crate boundaries.

evidence.claim: anyhow 1.0 is the standard for application code; never expose in library public APIs

candidates.decision_rationale: Keep; restrict to main.rs + CLI; convert library-code anyhow!() to UarError variants.

candidates.name: error-stack (Rust error context with frames)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Attach source chain + frames to errors; structured context; pairs with thiserror.

evidence.claim: error-stack is Hash's production error-context crate; provides Report<T> with frames

risks: Some overlap with thiserror's #[source]; pick one to wrap the other
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; wrap UarError in Report for context; surface frames in miette diagnostic.

candidates.name: tracing-error (tracing span to error chain)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Bridges tracing spans to error chains; ensures request_id / agent_id / run_id context flows with errors.

evidence.claim: tracing-error bridges tracing spans to error chains via SpanTrace

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; ensure every UarError carries the current span trace.

candidates.name: sentry-sdk (production observability)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Production error observability; pairs with tracing-error; optional but standard for production runtimes.

evidence.claim: sentry-rust is the standard Rust Sentry SDK; pairs with tracing

risks: Network dependency; behind a feature flag
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt behind --features sentry; default off.

candidates.name: cargo-llvm-cov
candidates.fit_for_gap: Code coverage measurement in CI; --fail-under-lines 80; recommended over tarpaulin.

evidence.claim: cargo-llvm-cov is the recommended Rust coverage tool; uses LLVM source-based instrumentation; --fail-under-lines supported; works on Linux/macOS/Windows via nightly

risks: Requires nightly; CI job can install automatically
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; replace the .grcovrc with cargo-llvm-cov in CI; Codecov for the dashboard.

candidates.name: cargo-mutants
candidates.fit_for_gap: Mutation testing; measures test quality; nightly CI job.

evidence.claim: cargo-mutants is the standard Rust mutation tester; sourcefrog maintains

risks: Slow on 68K LOC; nightly schedule only
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; nightly cron; track mutation score over time.

candidates.name: proptest
candidates.fit_for_gap: Property-based testing; serde roundtrips, retrieval RRF invariants, governance policy hot-reload semantics.

evidence.claim: proptest is the standard Rust property-based testing library

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; add property tests for the 3 surfaces identified in §6.4.

candidates.name: cargo-fuzz
candidates.fit_for_gap: libFuzzer-backed fuzz testing; required for any surface accepting untrusted input (MCP, file_processing, RAG).

evidence.claim: cargo-fuzz is the standard Rust fuzzer; libFuzzer-backed; 24h corpus runs standard

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; 4 fuzz targets (chunker, RAG verification, MCP message parsing, JSON Schema validator).

candidates.name: release-plz
candidates.fit_for_gap: Conventional commits → SemVer → CHANGELOG → PR automation; replaces manual release notes.

evidence.claim: release-plz is the standard Rust release automation; conventional commits → SemVer → CHANGELOG → PR

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; add commitlint + lefthook for the JS workspace.

candidates.name: cargo-deny
candidates.fit_for_gap: License + advisory + ban + sources gate; complements UAR's security audit.

evidence.claim: cargo-deny is the standard Rust dependency policy gate; license + advisory + ban + sources

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; configure for the new license targets (§8).

candidates.name: slsa-github-generator (SLSA Level 3 reusable workflow)
candidates.fit_for_gap: SLSA L3 self-attestation; signing in isolated job, separate from build workflow.

evidence.claim: SLSA 3 Container Generator for GitHub Actions is GA; free; produces L3-compliant provenance signed by cosign in an isolated job
GitHub Artifact Attestations: L2 by default, L3 by using a reusable workflow that runs signing on dedicated infrastructure

risks: Sensitive to runner environment; first integration may flake
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; add a provenance.yml reusable workflow that runs after every release build.

candidates.name: actions/attest-sbom (GitHub first-party)
candidates.fit_for_gap: First-party SBOM attestation alongside the SLSA provenance; pairs with syft-generated SBOM.

evidence.claim: actions/attest-sbom is the first-party SBOM attestation step

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; pair with slsa-github-generator.

candidates.name: osv-scanner + grype (continuous vuln scanning)
candidates.fit_for_gap: SBOM-based vulnerability scanning in CI; nightly; block on CVE ≥ HIGH for published artifacts.

evidence.claim: osv-scanner + grype are the standard SBOM-based vulnerability scanners

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; nightly cron; block on HIGH+ for published artifacts.

candidates.name: slsa-verifier
candidates.fit_for_gap: CLI verification of SLSA provenance; the official verifier; ships with slsa-github-generator.

evidence.claim: slsa-verifier is the official SLSA provenance verifier

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; wire into the candidate-certification workflow as the verification step.

candidates.name: MIT License (Text)
candidates.fit_for_gap: MIT for SDKs to match LangChain/LangGraph/CrewAI/MAF/OpenAI Agents SDK/LlamaIndex/Haystack/Markus.

evidence.claim: MIT is the dominant SDK license in the 2026 OSS agent ecosystem

risks: No patent grant; no NOTICE file requirement
candidates.decision_rationale: Recommended for SDKs. Contested with Apache-2.0 — see §12.1.

candidates.name: Apache-2.0 License (Text)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Apache-2.0 for SDKs if patent clarity is needed; matches agentgateway and the Rust ecosystem (Tokio, axum).

evidence.claim: Apache-2.0 is the dominant Rust ecosystem license; explicit patent grant

candidates.decision_rationale: Strong alternative to MIT for SDKs if patent clarity matters; the right answer for the runtime if a permissive license is ever considered.

candidates.name: AGPL-3.0 + Commercial dual-license (Markus precedent)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Server-side copyleft preserves the OSS moat; commercial band gives SaaS deployers an exit; matches Markus precedent.

evidence.claim: Markus (AGPL-3.0 + commercial) is the only copyleft entrant in the agent-company-platform comparison; pricing is public

risks: Commercial terms must be publicly published with pricing bands
candidates.decision_rationale: Recommended for the runtime server; preserves the copyleft moat.

risks: Heavier than Histoire; Histoire alternative if Vite-native is preferred
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; integrate with the existing frontend workspace.

candidates.name: Hosted rustdoc + typedoc pipeline

evidence.claim: rustdoc + cargo doc --no-deps is the standard Rust API doc pipeline

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; gh-pages deploy; typedoc for the TS SDK.

candidates.name: Docusaurus (already in website/, mature it)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Existing docs site; mature with the new cookbook, A2UI Inspector, and ADRs.

evidence.claim: Docusaurus is the standard OSS docs site; UAR already uses it (website/)

candidates.decision_rationale: Keep; expand with the new content from §9.

candidates.name: vale.sh (prose lint)
candidates.fit_for_gap: Prose lint for consistent terminology across docs/.

evidence.claim: vale is the standard prose linter; CI-friendly; project rules + vocab

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; ship a UAR-specific style config.

risks: v1.0-rc still iterating; pin to a specific version

candidates.fit_for_gap: WCAG 2.2 AA accessible React primitives; the 2026 gold standard; powers the A2UI component catalog.

evidence.claim: react-aria-components provides WCAG-compliant React primitives; 2026 default for accessibility-first React libraries

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt as the a11y substrate for the UAR A2UI catalog.

candidates.name: motion (formerly Framer Motion) for animation

evidence.claim: motion (formerly Framer Motion) is the 2026 standard for declarative React animation

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; use for streaming-update transitions and entrance/exit animations.

evidence.claim: quicktype is the standard schema-to-types codegen tool; supports JSON Schema → TypeScript

risks: Quicktype's TS output can be verbose; consider generating OpenAPI instead and using openapi-typescript
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; codegen A2UI TS types in a pre-build step.

candidates.fit_for_gap: Already in the UAR React/Tailwind stack; provides the catalog base (Button, Card, CheckBox, etc.).

evidence.claim: shadcn/ui is the de-facto React 19 + Tailwind + Radix component baseline in 2026

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; use as the catalog base for the A2UI component library.

candidates.name: cmdk (command-menu UI)
candidates.fit_for_gap: The ChoicePicker A2UI component for large option lists; the 2026 best command-menu UI in React.

evidence.claim: cmdk is the 2026 standard for command-menu UIs in React

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt for ChoicePicker with > 20 options.

candidates.name: react-hook-form + zod resolver
candidates.fit_for_gap: Form state + validation for the Form A2UI component; the 2026 de-facto form stack.

evidence.claim: react-hook-form + zod is the 2026 de-facto React form stack

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; pair with zod (§2.3) for schema-driven form validation.

candidates.name: @tanstack/react-virtual
candidates.fit_for_gap: List virtualization for the Form A2UI component with many fields; the 2026 standard.

evidence.claim: @tanstack/react-virtual is the 2026 standard for list virtualization in React

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt for large forms (> 50 fields).

candidates.name: @internationalized/string + react-aria i18n
candidates.fit_for_gap: i18n framework for the A2UI library; l10n strings + RTL support.

evidence.claim: @internationalized/* is the standard i18n stack for React Aria components

candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt; ship en, es, ja, zh; RTL framework.

build_required.need: Central pub enum UarError (#[non_exhaustive]) per public module surface
build_required.why_no_candidate: Domain-specific; requires design decision per UAR module boundary

build_required.need: Citation stream (Rust SSE type + React renderer component)
build_required.why_no_candidate: Requires the UAR RAG retrieval integration; no off-the-shelf component ships per-chunk citation UX at this fidelity

build_required.need: A2UI Inspector (devtools app for SSE message inspection)
build_required.why_no_candidate: No A2UI devtools exists upstream; Google has not shipped @a2ui/inspector; the deliverable is UAR-specific

build_required.need: UAR-specific A2UI component catalog (≥ 14 components with animations + a11y)
build_required.why_no_candidate: UAR's approved catalog is more restrictive than Google's; mapping work is required

build_required.need: A2UI ↔ AG-UI bridge (typed event mapping + live-update transitions)
build_required.why_no_candidate: UAR's AG-UI event model is the source of truth; the bridge is UAR-specific

build_required.need: prometheus-eval (golden set + judge prompt harness for RAG evaluation)
build_required.why_no_candidate: Project-specific golden set; 300 items spanning UAR's 5 primary intents

build_required.need: Cookbook (12 runnable examples spanning runtime + SDKs + A2UI)
build_required.why_no_candidate: UAR-specific examples; not adoptable from a library

open_questions.question: SDK license: MIT, BSD-3-Clause, or Apache-2.0?
open_questions.recommendation: MIT (matches 8/8 named competitor SDKs) or Apache-2.0 (if patent clarity matters)

open_questions.question: A2UI React renderer: vendor Google's @a2ui/react or build UAR-owned on @a2ui/web_core?
open_questions.recommendation: Vendor @a2ui/web_core; build UAR-owned React renderer on top; cross-test against @a2ui/react as reference impl.

open_questions.question: Relicensing approach: open letter to SDK contributors, CLA going forward, or clean-history split?
open_questions.recommendation: Open letter for SDKs (small surface, ~10 known contributors) + clean-history split for runtime

open_questions.question: Coverage gate threshold: 60% or 80% on day one?
open_questions.recommendation: Start at 60%; grow quarterly to 80% as the test surface matures

open_questions.question: Property-test / fuzz-test budget: minimum (22h) or follow-up-grade (60+h)?
open_questions.recommendation: Minimum 22h; schedule a follow-up-grade fuzz pass after the grade-A cut
